description: In the file finder, a stale content response from a superseded keystroke never lands. The conversation /c/{{SLUG}} runs in a git repository holding (untracked) paprika-notes.txt, which reads "cardamom goes well here", and other.txt, which reads "nothing relevant". The server's answer to the FIRST content-search request (GET /api/find-files with content=only) is held back until call "release"; every other request passes. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. 2. Open the fuzzy file finder by pressing "p" (lowercase) with the Control modifier, without clicking anything first, and wait up to 10s for its input ".grp-filter" to be visible. 3. Fill the finder input with "cardamom". 4. ".ff-grep-pending" should become visible (up to 10s): that keystroke's content search is now stuck. 5. Fill the finder input with "paprika" (this supersedes it; its own phases both land). 6. There should come to be exactly 1 ".grp-row" (up to 10s), containing "paprika-notes.txt". 7. Call "release". 8. Sleep 300ms to give the stale response a beat to (not) apply. 9. There must still be exactly 1 ".grp-row", and exactly 0 ".ff-snippet" elements.
